idf.context_text: The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) is Israel's military, encompassing army, navy, and air force branches under a unified command structure. Since October 2023 it has conducted a sustained military campaign in Gaza and, since March 2026, an expanded campaign in southern Lebanon against Hezbollah, alongside continued operations in the occupied West Bank. A UN commission of inquiry concluded in mid-2026 that the IDF has deliberately targeted children in Gaza, a finding the Israeli government disputes. The IDF operates under civilian government direction but has at times publicly signaled disagreement with government decisions on ceasefire enforcement and troop withdrawal timelines.

hezbollah.context_text: Hezbollah is a Lebanese Shia Islamist political party and armed movement founded in 1982 during Israel's occupation of southern Lebanon, with longstanding backing from Iran. It holds seats in the Lebanese parliament and maintains an armed force historically outside state control, which the United States, Israel and other governments designate a terrorist organization. Founding leader Hassan Nasrallah was killed in an Israeli strike on Beirut in September 2024; Naim Qassem has led the group since. Under a mid-2026 US-brokered framework between Lebanon and Israel, Hezbollah is not a direct party but faces demands to disarm as Israeli forces gradually withdraw from the south.

unifil.full_name: United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon

netanyahu.context_text: Benjamin Netanyahu is Israel's Prime Minister, the longest-serving in the country's history, heading a coalition government dependent on far-right and religious parties including Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism. He faces an outstanding International Criminal Court arrest warrant, issued in November 2024, over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza, and continues to stand trial domestically on corruption charges. Netanyahu has publicly committed to Hamas's total defeat while simultaneously negotiating phased ceasefire and disarmament frameworks with US mediation.

trump.context_text: Donald Trump is the 47th President of the United States, having returned to office in January 2025 after a first term from 2017-2021. His administration has pursued a 20-point plan for ending the Gaza war, brokered through what it calls the Board of Peace, an international body intended to oversee Gaza's postwar governance and reconstruction. Trump has repeatedly claimed personal credit for regional ceasefires, including the October 2025 Gaza truce and the mid-2026 US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding, while facing skepticism from allies and adversaries over enforcement. He has framed continued US support for Israel as conditional on progress toward ending the war.

pezeshkian.context_text: Masoud Pezeshkian is a cardiac surgeon and reformist politician who has served as President of Iran since July 2024, after previously serving as health minister under President Khatami (2001-2005) and as a member of parliament from 2008. He favours negotiated agreements with the West, though his authority is ultimately subordinate to Iran's Supreme Leader. Iran has been at war with the United States and Israel since February 2026; Pezeshkian negotiated and has publicly defended a June 2026 memorandum of understanding with Washington against hardline domestic critics who accused him of making concessions, while also arguing Tehran now holds the stronger negotiating position.

smotrich.context_text: Bezalel Smotrich is Israel's Finance Minister and leader of the far-right Religious Zionism party, in the Knesset since 2015. Born in 1980, he is a West Bank settler who has built his political career on the position that the West Bank and Gaza rightfully belong to the Jewish people and has opposed Palestinian statehood. As an additional minister within the Defence Ministry he oversees the Settlement Administration, which controls land, planning and settlement development in the occupied West Bank. He faces an ICC prosecutor's request for an arrest warrant over forced-displacement orders and settler-expansion policy, and has repeatedly linked settlement construction, including the E1 project, to preventing establishment of a Palestinian state.

ben-gvir.context_text: Itamar Ben-Gvir is Israel's National Security Minister and leader of the far-right Otzma Yehudit (Jewish Power) party, part of Netanyahu's governing coalition since December 2022. A former disciple of the outlawed Kach movement, once convicted of incitement to racism and supporting a terrorist organization, he has built his political career on hardline positions toward Palestinians, including expanded settlement construction and weakened use-of-force restrictions for police and soldiers. He has repeatedly threatened to collapse the governing coalition over ceasefire and peace-plan concessions he views as insufficiently punitive toward Hamas.

israel-katz.context_text: Israel Katz (b. 1955, Ashkelon) is an Israeli Likud politician and member of the Knesset since 1998, previously holding the Foreign Affairs, Finance, Energy, Transport, and Intelligence portfolios. Netanyahu appointed him Defense Minister on 5 November 2024 after dismissing Yoav Gallant. Israeli media have described Katz, seen as close and loyal to Netanyahu, as a 'bulldozer' for his combative political style.

francesca-albanese.context_text: Francesca Albanese is an Italian international lawyer who has served as UN Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the Palestinian territories occupied since 1967 since May 2022. She has authored reports characterizing Israeli conduct in Gaza as genocide and has been a prominent international legal voice calling for an arms embargo on Israel. The US State Department sanctioned her in 2025 over her criticism of Israel and the United States; the sanctions were lifted in 2026 after a federal judge found they restricted her free speech.

hrw.context_text: Human Rights Watch (HRW) is an international non-governmental organization founded in 1978, headquartered in New York, that investigates and reports on human rights abuses worldwide. Its Israel-Palestine research has documented settler violence, military conduct in the West Bank and Gaza, and occupation-related policy.

khalil-al-hayya.context_text: Khalil al-Hayya is the newly elected head of Hamas's political bureau, chosen by the group's General Shura Council on 20 July 2026 in a run-off vote against former political chief Khaled Meshaal. He succeeds Yahya Sinwar, killed by the Israeli army in Gaza in 2024. He has long been a senior Hamas figure involved in ceasefire and prisoner-exchange negotiations.

ro-khanna.context_text: Ro Khanna is a Democratic member of the US House of Representatives representing a Silicon Valley district in California, first elected in 2016. He has been an outspoken critic of US military aid to Israel and has visited the occupied West Bank on congressional delegations.

zohran-mamdani.context_text: Zohran Mamdani is a Democratic Socialist who was sworn in as Mayor of New York City on 1 January 2026, becoming the city's first Muslim mayor and first of South Asian descent after previously representing Queens in the New York State Assembly. A vocal critic of Israeli conduct in Gaza throughout his campaign and tenure, he has called for enforcement of the International Criminal Court's arrest warrant against Netanyahu on US soil.

volker-turk.context_text: Volker Türk is an Austrian human rights lawyer who has served as UN High Commissioner for Human Rights since October 2022, the UN's top human rights official, based in Geneva. He has repeatedly warned that Israeli military conduct in Gaza and Lebanon — including demolitions of civilian infrastructure and forced population displacement — may amount to war crimes under international humanitarian law.

yinon-levi.context_text: Yinon Levi is an Israeli settler identified by the Palestinian rights group Al-Haq as the man who fatally shot Palestinian activist Awdah Hathaleen in the West Bank village of Umm al-Khair on 28 July 2025. He runs the illegal Meitarim Farm outpost in the South Hebron Hills and has drawn manpower from Hashomer Yosh, a settler group that supplies volunteers to such outposts. He was not arrested at the scene and was later released to a three-day house arrest.

al-haq.context_text: Al-Haq is a Palestinian human rights organization based in Ramallah, founded in 1979, that documents human rights violations in the occupied Palestinian territories and pursues international legal accountability, including submissions to the International Criminal Court. Its investigations combine video and photographic evidence, legal testimony, and geospatial and open-source analysis.

awdah-hathaleen.context_text: Awdah Hathaleen was a 31-year-old Palestinian activist and father of three from the village of Umm al-Khair in Masafer Yatta, in the South Hebron Hills of the occupied West Bank. He had worked on production of the Oscar-winning documentary 'No Other Land' and was filming an armed settler raid on his village when he was shot and killed on 28 July 2025.

amnesty-international.context_text: Amnesty International is a London-headquartered international human rights organization founded in 1961 that investigates and campaigns against human rights abuses worldwide, including through detailed documentation of arms transfers and their end use. It has published a series of reports since 2023 tracking foreign military supply chains feeding Israel's campaign in Gaza, which it characterizes as genocide.

agnes-callamard.context_text: Agnès Callamard is a French human rights lawyer who has served as Secretary General of Amnesty International since 2021, after previously serving as UN Special Rapporteur on extrajudicial executions. Under her leadership Amnesty has published reports alleging that Israel's conduct in Gaza meets the legal threshold of genocide and has pressed states and companies supplying Israel's military to halt arms transfers.

global-affairs-canada.context_text: Global Affairs Canada is the Canadian federal department responsible for foreign policy, diplomatic relations, and international trade. It has periodically criticized Israeli settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank as a violation of international law, though critics note Ottawa has rarely followed such statements with concrete policy measures against Israel.

ohchr.full_name: Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
ohchr.context_text: The Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), headed by Volker Türk, is the principal United Nations entity mandated to promote and protect human rights globally. It regularly documents and reports on Israeli settlement expansion and settler violence in the occupied West Bank, drawing on UN field monitoring data.

gadi-eisenkot.context_text: Gadi Eisenkot is a retired Israeli general who served as IDF Chief of Staff from 2015 to 2019, during which he developed the 'Dahieh Doctrine' calling for disproportionate force to establish deterrence against Hezbollah. He joined Netanyahu's war cabinet as a non-voting observer during the Gaza war's first year before resigning in June 2024 in protest of the government's conduct, having lost his own son and nephew in the fighting. He has since emerged as a leading contender to replace Netanyahu, positioning himself as a critic of the government's failure to secure a decisive end to the conflict.

ghazi-hamad.context_text: Ghazi Hamad is a senior Hamas political bureau member and one of the movement's principal negotiators in ceasefire and prisoner-exchange talks. Born in 1964 in the Yibna refugee camp, he trained as a veterinarian before becoming a journalist and later a Hamas official, previously serving as the group's deputy foreign minister and head of the Gaza-Egypt border crossing authority. He left Gaza for Lebanon shortly before the October 2023 Hamas attack on Israel that triggered the war, and has represented Hamas's position in international media as disarmament became a central sticking point in negotiations.

nickolay-mladenov.context_text: Nickolay Mladenov is a Bulgarian diplomat and former Bulgarian foreign and defense minister who served as UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process from 2015 to 2020, working extensively with Israeli, Palestinian Authority, and Hamas officials. In January 2026 the Trump administration and Israel named him director-general of the Board of Peace, the international body established to oversee Gaza's postwar governance, weapons decommissioning, and reconstruction. He has cultivated a reputation for balanced engagement with both sides and has stressed that the disarmament roadmap's implementation and verification mechanisms matter more than the agreement's announcement.

kaja-kallas.context_text: Kaja Kallas is a former Prime Minister of Estonia (2021-2024) who has served since December 2024 as the European Union's High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy and a Vice-President of the European Commission, the bloc's most senior foreign policy post. The daughter of former Estonian Prime Minister Siim Kallas, she built her earlier career as a lawyer and MEP focused on digital markets and competition law. As EU foreign policy chief she has been a prominent voice on Ukraine and has offered cautious, conditional statements on Israel-Palestine developments.

nawaf-salam.context_text: Nawaf Salam is the Prime Minister of Lebanon, in office since February 2025. A member of a prominent Beirut Sunni political family, he holds law and political science doctorates from Harvard and Sciences Po and served as Lebanon's ambassador to the United Nations from 2007 to 2017 before sitting on the International Court of Justice, where he was elected president in 2024. As prime minister he has repeatedly protested Israeli military activity in southern Lebanon as violations of the ceasefire announced in mid-2026, while lacking direct authority over Hezbollah, whose disarmament remains a central unresolved issue in Lebanese politics.

rashida-tlaib.context_text: Rashida Tlaib is a Democratic member of the US House of Representatives representing Michigan's 12th congressional district, first elected in 2018 as the first Palestinian American woman in Congress. A member of the progressive bloc of lawmakers known as 'the Squad,' she has been one of Congress's most vocal critics of Israeli government policy in Gaza and the West Bank, while stating that criticism of Israeli occupation and military conduct is not equivalent to antisemitism.

michael-gottlieb.context_text: Michael Gottlieb is a Democratic member of the Florida House of Representatives, representing the state's 102nd district in the Fort Lauderdale area, and a criminal defense lawyer by profession. He chairs the Florida Legislative Jewish Caucus and has previously issued statements responding to antisemitic incidents in South Florida's Jewish community.

ed-miliband.context_text: Ed Miliband is a British Labour Party politician who has served as the UK's Foreign Secretary since 2024, after previously serving as Energy Secretary and as Labour Party leader from 2010 to 2015. The son of Marxist theorist Ralph Miliband, he has held a Doncaster parliamentary seat since 2005. In August 2026 he announced the UK had summoned Israel's chargé d'affaires and demanded reversal of construction tenders for the E1 West Bank settlement project, joining a joint condemnation of the plan issued with France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Canada and Norway.

ir-amim.context_text: Ir Amim is an Israeli NGO, founded in 2000, that monitors and challenges Israeli policy in Jerusalem and the West Bank, focused on the impact of settlement expansion on the prospects for a negotiated resolution of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. It has pursued legal challenges to the E1 settlement project alongside Peace Now and Bimkom, and said in August 2026 that Israel's government had published new E1 construction tenders despite a pending Jerusalem District Court case and without notifying petitioners as it had previously committed to do.

ubai-al-aboudi.context_text: Ubai al-Aboudi is a Palestinian human rights advocate who has publicly assessed the E1 settlement project and international responses to Israeli settlement expansion. He has said the E1 project would put a 'final nail in the coffin' of the two-state solution, and has criticized Western governments' condemnations of settlement expansion as 'lip service with little action,' arguing that international impunity has allowed Israel to continue advancing settlement construction on the ground despite verbal objections.

ines-abdel-razek.context_text: Ines Abdel Razek is co-director of the Palestine Institute for Public Diplomacy. Commenting on international condemnation of Israel's E1 settlement tenders in August 2026, she argued that Western governments' references to a threatened 'two-state solution' function as diplomatic rhetoric covering inaction and complicity in Palestinian dispossession, pointing to the destruction of Gaza's civilian infrastructure and displacement of two million people alongside the West Bank's continuing annexation as evidence the prospect had already been foreclosed.

tom-barrack.context_text: Tom Barrack is a Lebanese-American billionaire investor, founder of the private equity firm Colony Capital (now DigitalBridge), and a longtime ally of President Trump who chaired his 2017 inauguration committee. Trump named him US Ambassador to Turkey in 2025 and Special Envoy for Syria the same year, later adding the Iraq envoy role in January 2026. In that capacity he has criticized Israeli military actions in Syria, including a strike on the Abu al-Duhur airbase, warning they could provoke direct confrontation with Turkey, and has publicly diverged from official US recognition of Israeli sovereignty over the Golan Heights.

erdogan.context_text: Recep Tayyip Erdogan is President of Turkey, in office since 2014 after previously serving as prime minister from 2003. His government has been among the most vocal critics of Israel's conduct in Gaza and the West Bank, and in August 2026 Turkey's Justice Ministry sought an Interpol arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu over the May 2026 interception of a Gaza-bound flotilla. Netanyahu responded by publicly calling Erdogan an antisemitic dictator who has 'massacred Kurds,' occupies part of Cyprus and jails political opponents and journalists.

akin-gurlek.context_text: Akin Gurlek is Turkey's Justice Minister. In August 2026 he announced that Turkey was seeking an Interpol red notice for the arrest of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, tied to an Istanbul court case trying 35 defendants in absentia over Israel's May 2026 naval interception of a flotilla attempting to break the blockade of Gaza, on charges including genocide, other crimes against humanity, torture, unlawful detention and hijacking.

yesh-din.context_text: Yesh Din is an Israeli human rights organization, founded in 2005, that monitors and documents human rights violations against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank, including settler violence, military conduct and land expropriation, and pursues legal accountability through the Israeli court system. In an August 2026 report titled 'The Next Frontier,' the group found that settler violence had begun shifting from rural areas toward larger, more populated Palestinian cities and towns, a pattern it linked to the government's approval of new settlements and the expansion of unauthorized outposts that authorities have largely left in place.
